# A PURE BASE MERGE (archived issue 795, owner decision 2026-10-07): NEW is a merge
# commit whose first parent is OLD -- the head that carried `ready` --
# whose second parent is already on the base branch, and whose tree is
# exactly the merge of the two. That is what GitHub's "Update branch"
# makes, and nothing in it is a change anybody has to review again.
# Read in a scratch bare repository: commits and trees fetched by sha,
# the blobs merge-tree needs fetched on demand, nothing checked out and
# nothing run. 0: pure. 1: anything else. 2: could not tell.
is_pure_base_merge() {
  local old="$1" new="$2" repo line second merged tree rc=0
  local -a parents
  [[ "${old}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "${new}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || return 2
  repo="$(mktemp -d)"
  git init -q --bare "${repo}" || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" config credential.helper '!gh auth git-credential' || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" remote add origin "${REMOTE_URL}" || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" fetch -q --no-tags --filter=blob:none origin \
    "${new}" "+refs/heads/${BASE_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/base" || return 2
  line="$(git -C "${repo}" rev-list --parents -n 1 "${new}")" || return 2
  read -r -a parents <<<"${line}"
  [[ "${#parents[@]}" -eq 3 && "${parents[1]}" == "${old}" ]] || return 1
  second="${parents[2]}"
  git -C "${repo}" merge-base --is-ancestor "${second}" refs/remotes/origin/base || return 1
  merged="$(git -C "${repo}" merge-tree --write-tree "${old}" "${second}")" || rc=$?
  if [[ "${rc}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    return 1
  elif [[ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  tree="$(git -C "${repo}" rev-parse "${new}^{tree}")" || return 2
  [[ "${merged%%$'\n'*}" == "${tree}" ]] || return 1
}

#    title (and through a merge queue, the merge commit's message
#    carries it), so queuing this would put "[swarm] task_..." on
#    main -- the archived pull request 238 defect with a different string. Quoted, so
#    the prefix is literal: an unquoted [swarm] is a glob bracket
#    expression matching one character. Case- and leading-whitespace-
#    insensitive: "[Swarm] task_" or "  [swarm] task_" is still the

#    branch's EFFECTIVE rules -- every ruleset that applies, via
#    `rules/branches/{branch}` -- and classic protection's checks,
#    unique by name, so a repository that moves back to classic
#    protection still counts. Paginated: the rules list is a page of
#    rules, and `jq -s add` joins however many pages come back.

gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/branches/${BASE_REF}" >"${branch}"
rules="$(mktemp)"
gh api --paginate "repos/${GH_REPO}/rules/branches/${BASE_REF}?per_page=100" >"${rules}"

{
  jq -r '(.protection.required_status_checks.contexts // [])[],
         ((.protection.required_status_checks.checks // [])[] | .context)' "${branch}"
  jq -rs 'add // [] | .[]
          | select(.type == "required_status_checks")
          | (.parameters.required_status_checks // [])[] | .context' "${rules}"
} >"${required_names}"

fi

#    step enqueues there instead of squashing (docs/ci.md "Merging
#    through the merge queue"). Same rules read as above.
queue="$(jq -rs 'add // [] | any(.[]; .type == "merge_queue")' "${rules}")"

#    the merge too, even when it is not one of the required checks

#    pull request (docs/ci.md); a path-filtered workflow such as
#    application.yml or terraform.yml is not required, but when a
#    pull request's changes DO trigger it, its result is still real
#    signal auto-merge must not ignore. A failing check refuses at
#    once, even beside running ones: waiting cannot make it green.

#    auto-merge"), which is always still `in_progress` here.
#    A check is judged by the LATEST run of EACH event that ran it

#    merge step's `latest_per_event` judges it: a re-run replaces
#    the earlier runs of its own event, never another's, so a red
#    push run is not outvoted by a green pull_request run

#    suite, read from the Actions runs at the head only when some
#    check has more than one run; a suite with no known event is
#    its own group, so one suite never outvotes another.
#    A run has finished when its status is completed, OR when it
#    carries a conclusion together with a completed_at, whatever
#    its status says (the owner, 2026-10-23, CHECK-STUCK, part of archived issue 2031):
#    GitHub left PR 2006's `secret scan` at in_progress with
#    conclusion success and a completed_at. The worker's
#    `check_run_finished` and `merge-train.sh judge` say the same.
#    A latest run that was CANCELLED is not failing (archived issue 1778, the owner's
#    bundle H09, 2026-10-27): it is pending, and gate 6 waits on it
#    when the check is required, as on one still running.
runs="$(mktemp)"
gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/check-runs?per_page=100" >"${runs}"
wf_runs="$(mktemp)"
printf '{"workflow_runs": []}\n' >"${wf_runs}"
if jq -e '[.check_runs[].name] | group_by(.) | any(length > 1)' "${runs}" >/dev/null; then
  gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/actions/runs?head_sha=${HEAD_SHA}&per_page=100" >"${wf_runs}"
fi

# here and gate 6 below (CHECK-RULE-2, part of archived issue 1999).
latest="$(mktemp)"
jq --slurpfile wf "${wf_runs}" '
    ([ $wf[0].workflow_runs[]?
       | select(.check_suite_id != null and (.event // "") != "")
       | {key: (.check_suite_id | tostring), value: .event} ]
     | from_entries) as $events
    | [ .check_runs[]
        | select(.name != "queue for auto-merge")
        | . + {group: ($events[(.check_suite.id // "" | tostring)]
                      // "check suite \(.check_suite.id // "")")} ]
    | group_by([.name, .group])
    | map(max_by(.id))' "${runs}" >"${latest}"
failing="$(jq -r '
    def finished: .status == "completed"
                  or ((.conclusion // "") != "" and (.completed_at // "") != "");
    [ .[]
      | select(finished)
      | select((.conclusion // "") as $c |
               $c == "failure" or $c == "timed_out" or
               $c == "action_required")
      | .name
    ] | unique | join(", ")' "${latest}")"
if [[ -n "${failing}" ]]; then
  refuse "This check already ran on the head commit and is failing: ${failing}. A failed check holds the merge, required or not."
fi

# 5b. THE MERGE TRAIN HAS IT (owner decision 2026-10-14, "A1 Merge
#    train"). With vars.MERGE_TRAIN `on`, .github/workflows/
#    merge-train.yml boards `ready` pull requests that are green at
#    head, tests them together on main and lands each as its own
#    squash; arming native auto-merge as well would merge them one
#    at a time, untested together, around it. So after every refusal
#    above (a failing check still drops `ready` on a re-evaluation,
#    and the train boards none that fails), nothing is armed: said
#    once, on the label. A re-evaluation says nothing more. Exactly
#    `on`: anything else is the train off, and this gate unchanged.
if [[ "${MERGE_TRAIN:-}" == "on" ]]; then
  echo "decision=train" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Left to the merge train.** Auto-merge is not armed: once this pull request is green at its head, \`.github/workflows/merge-train.yml\` boards it with other \`ready\` pull requests, tests them together on main, and squash-merges each under its title. A push drops \`ready\` unless it only merges the base branch in."
    echo "(.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml; docs/runbooks/merge-train.md)"
  } >"${body}"
  if [[ "${reevaluation}" != "true" ]]; then
    gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --body-file "${body}"
  fi
  {
    echo "### Left to the merge train"
    echo
    cat "${body}"
  } >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
  exit 0
fi

# 6. A REQUIRED check still running WAITS (archived pull request 697). Nothing is armed:
#    the `requeue` job re-evaluates when each run or check suite
#    finishes on this head, and the last one merges it. Said once,
#    on the label; a re-evaluation that still waits says nothing.
#    Only a required one (archived issue 815): a non-required check still running
#    -- code scanning's `Trivy` held archived pull request 811 for five hours -- is not
#    something the ruleset waits for, so it does not hold the
#    merge either. Required means item 3's names, the ruleset's and
#    classic protection's. Native auto-merge, armed below, still
#    waits for every required check, so one not yet reported at all
#    holds the merge there. A required check is read by its
#    latest run of each event, gate 5's deciding runs (the owner,
#    2026-10-22, "one rule for every check", CHECK-RULE-2, part of
#    archived issue 1999): a run still in progress that a later run of its own
#    event replaced does not hold the merge. A run is still
#    running until it has finished as gate 5 reads it (CHECK-STUCK,
#    part of archived issue 2031) AND carries a conclusion: one `completed` with
#    none is not green, so it waits too, and so does one whose
#    latest run was cancelled (archived issue 1778): a re-run, not a fix, is what
#    it is waiting for.
required_json="$(jq -Rs 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)) | unique' "${required_names}")"
unfinished="$(jq -r --argjson required "${required_json}" '
    def finished: .status == "completed"
                  or ((.conclusion // "") != "" and (.completed_at // "") != "");
    [ .[]
      | select((finished | not) or (.conclusion // "") == ""
               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
      | .name
      | select(. as $name | $required | index($name))
    ] | unique | join(", ")' "${latest}")"
if [[ -n "${unfinished}" ]]; then
  echo "decision=wait" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Queued for auto-merge, waiting for required checks still running on the head commit:** ${unfinished}."
    echo
    echo "It is re-evaluated each time an application or security run, or another App's check suite, finishes on this head (application's last job, ci-gate, waits for terraform), and merged once every required check is green and no check that ran has failed. A push drops \`ready\` unless it only merges the base branch in."
    echo "(.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml)"
  } >"${body}"
  if [[ "${reevaluation}" != "true" ]]; then
    gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --body-file "${body}"
  fi
  {
    echo "### Waiting"
    echo
    cat "${body}"
  } >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
  echo "waiting for: ${unfinished}"
  exit 0
fi

echo "queue=${queue}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
echo "decision=merge" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
echo "gate passed: ${required} required check(s) on ${BASE_REF}; merge queue: ${queue}"

merge.run:
set -euo pipefail
err="$(mktemp)"

# Merge states GitHub will merge now and will not arm auto-merge on:
# every required check passed (see ALREADY GREEN above). UNSTABLE
# also covers a non-required check that FAILED after the gate read
# the checks; the direct merge then goes through, as native
# auto-merge would have. Accepted under archived issue 815.
mergeable_now() {
  case "$1" in
    CLEAN | UNSTABLE | HAS_HOOKS) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# A PURE BASE MERGE (archived issue 795, owner decision 2026-10-07): NEW is a merge
# commit whose first parent is OLD -- the head that carried `ready` --
# whose second parent is already on the base branch, and whose tree is
# exactly the merge of the two. That is what GitHub's "Update branch"
# makes, and nothing in it is a change anybody has to review again.
# Read in a scratch bare repository: commits and trees fetched by sha,
# the blobs merge-tree needs fetched on demand, nothing checked out and
# nothing run. 0: pure. 1: anything else. 2: could not tell.
is_pure_base_merge() {
  local old="$1" new="$2" repo line second merged tree rc=0
  local -a parents
  [[ "${old}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "${new}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || return 2
  repo="$(mktemp -d)"
  git init -q --bare "${repo}" || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" config credential.helper '!gh auth git-credential' || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" remote add origin "${REMOTE_URL}" || return 2
  git -C "${repo}" fetch -q --no-tags --filter=blob:none origin \
    "${new}" "+refs/heads/${BASE_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/base" || return 2
  line="$(git -C "${repo}" rev-list --parents -n 1 "${new}")" || return 2
  read -r -a parents <<<"${line}"
  [[ "${#parents[@]}" -eq 3 && "${parents[1]}" == "${old}" ]] || return 1
  second="${parents[2]}"
  git -C "${repo}" merge-base --is-ancestor "${second}" refs/remotes/origin/base || return 1
  merged="$(git -C "${repo}" merge-tree --write-tree "${old}" "${second}")" || rc=$?
  if [[ "${rc}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    return 1
  elif [[ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  tree="$(git -C "${repo}" rev-parse "${new}^{tree}")" || return 2
  [[ "${merged%%$'\n'*}" == "${tree}" ]] || return 1
}

# GitHub refused the pin: did the head move while this run was queued
# (archived issue 795)? Not moved: 1, and the refusal is judged below as before.
# Moved by a pure base merge of the labelled head: HEAD_SHA becomes the
# new head and 0, so it is armed once more there. Moved by anything
# else: that head was never labelled, so nothing is armed and the run
# ends (the disable job removes `ready` for it).
follow_base_merge() {
  local view moved verdict=0
  view="$(mktemp)"
  gh pr view "${PR_NUMBER}" --json headRefOid >"${view}"
  moved="$(jq -r .headRefOid "${view}")"
  [[ "${moved}" != "${HEAD_SHA}" ]] || return 1
  is_pure_base_merge "${HEAD_SHA}" "${moved}" || verdict=$?
  if [[ "${verdict}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "the head moved from ${HEAD_SHA} to ${moved} by a merge of ${BASE_REF} alone: arming at ${moved}"
    HEAD_SHA="${moved}"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "${verdict}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    {
      echo "### Not queued for auto-merge"
      echo
      echo "#${PR_NUMBER}'s head moved from ${HEAD_SHA} to ${moved} after \`ready\`, by a push that is not a merge of ${BASE_REF} alone. That head was never labelled: it needs a new \`ready\`."
    } >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
    echo "::warning::not queued: the head moved to ${moved} by a push that is not a merge of ${BASE_REF} alone"
    exit 0
  fi
  cat "${err}" >&2
  echo "::error::the head moved from ${HEAD_SHA} to ${moved}, and whether that only merged ${BASE_REF} could not be read"
  exit 1
}

# One retry, never a loop: a head that moves again is judged below.
armed=false
retried=false
if [[ "${QUEUE:-false}" != "true" ]]; then
  while true; do
    if gh pr merge "${PR_NUMBER}" --auto --squash \
        --match-head-commit "${HEAD_SHA}" \
        --subject "${PR_TITLE} (#${PR_NUMBER})" 2>"${err}"; then
      armed=true
      break
    fi
    if [[ "${retried}" == "true" ]] || ! follow_base_merge; then
      break
    fi
    retried=true
  done
  if [[ "${armed}" == "true" ]]; then
    outcome="squash-merges when its required checks pass"
  else
    view="$(mktemp)"
    gh pr view "${PR_NUMBER}" --json state,mergeStateStatus,autoMergeRequest >"${view}"
    state="$(jq -r .mergeStateStatus "${view}")"
    if jq -e '.state == "MERGED"' "${view}" >/dev/null; then
      outcome="had already been merged"
    elif jq -e '.autoMergeRequest != null' "${view}" >/dev/null; then
      outcome="already had auto-merge enabled, and squash-merges when its required checks pass"
    else
      if ! mergeable_now "${state}"; then
        cat "${err}" >&2
        echo "::error::auto-merge was not enabled (merge state ${state})"
        exit 1
      fi
      gh pr merge "${PR_NUMBER}" --squash \
        --match-head-commit "${HEAD_SHA}" \
        --subject "${PR_TITLE} (#${PR_NUMBER})"
      outcome="was already green and was merged now"
    fi
  fi
else
  while true; do
    if gh pr merge "${PR_NUMBER}" --auto \
        --match-head-commit "${HEAD_SHA}" 2>"${err}"; then
      armed=true
      break
    fi
    if [[ "${retried}" == "true" ]] || ! follow_base_merge; then
      break
    fi
    retried=true
  done
  if [[ "${armed}" == "true" ]]; then
    outcome="joins main's merge queue when its required checks pass"
  else
    view="$(mktemp)"
    gh pr view "${PR_NUMBER}" --json id,state,mergeStateStatus,autoMergeRequest >"${view}"
    state="$(jq -r .mergeStateStatus "${view}")"
    in_queue="$(gh api graphql \
      -f query='query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $number: Int!) { repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) { pullRequest(number: $number) { isInMergeQueue } } }' \
      -f owner="${GH_REPO%%/*}" -f name="${GH_REPO#*/}" -F number="${PR_NUMBER}" \
      --jq .data.repository.pullRequest.isInMergeQueue)"
    if jq -e '.state == "MERGED"' "${view}" >/dev/null; then
      outcome="had already been merged"
    elif [[ "${in_queue}" == "true" ]]; then
      outcome="was already in main's merge queue"
    elif jq -e '.autoMergeRequest != null' "${view}" >/dev/null; then
      outcome="already had auto-merge enabled, and joins main's merge queue when its required checks pass"
    else
      if ! mergeable_now "${state}"; then
        cat "${err}" >&2
        echo "::error::auto-merge was not enabled and the pull request was not enqueued (merge state ${state})"
        exit 1
      fi
      gh api graphql \
        -f query='mutation($id: ID!, $head: GitObjectID!) { enqueuePullRequest(input: {pullRequestId: $id, expectedHeadOid: $head}) { mergeQueueEntry { position } } }' \
        -f id="$(jq -r .id "${view}")" -f head="${HEAD_SHA}" >/dev/null
      outcome="was already green and was added to main's merge queue now"
    fi
  fi
fi
{
  echo "### Queued for auto-merge"
  echo
  echo "#${PR_NUMBER} ${outcome}, under:"
  echo
  echo "    ${PR_TITLE} (#${PR_NUMBER})"
  if [[ "${retried}" == "true" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "Pinned to ${HEAD_SHA}: the labelled head with ${BASE_REF} merged into it, and nothing else."
  fi
} >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"

pr.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ "${EVENT_NAME}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  if [[ ! "${PR_NUMBER}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "::error::the pr input is not a pull request number: ${PR_NUMBER}"
    exit 1
  fi
  view="$(mktemp)"
  gh pr view "${PR_NUMBER}" --json state,title,baseRefName,headRefOid,labels >"${view}"
  if ! jq -e '.state == "OPEN" and any(.labels[]; .name == "ready")' "${view}" >/dev/null; then
    echo "evaluate=false" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
    echo "#${PR_NUMBER} is not an open pull request labelled \`ready\`: nothing to re-evaluate." >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
    exit 0
  fi
  title="$(jq -r .title "${view}")"
  base_ref="$(jq -r .baseRefName "${view}")"
  head_sha="$(jq -r .headRefOid "${view}")"
else
  title="${EVENT_TITLE}"
  base_ref="${EVENT_BASE_REF}"
  head_sha="${EVENT_HEAD_SHA}"
fi
# The title is the author's text: written as a delimited block with
# a random delimiter, so no line of it can set another output.
delimiter="TITLE_$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
{
  echo "evaluate=true"
  echo "title<<${delimiter}"
  printf '%s\n' "${title}"
  echo "${delimiter}"
  echo "base_ref=${base_ref}"
  echo "head_sha=${head_sha}"
} >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

judge.run:
set -euo pipefail
work="$(mktemp -d)"
prs="${work}/prs.json"
gh pr list --state open --label ready-on-green --limit 200 \
  --json number,title,headRefOid,baseRefName >"${prs}"
candidates="${work}/candidates.tsv"
case "${EVENT_NAME}" in
  schedule) only_sha="" ;;
  *)
    if [[ -z "${RUN_HEAD_SHA}" ]]; then
      echo "no head sha on this ${EVENT_NAME} event: nothing to judge" | tee -a "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
      echo "promote=" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
      exit 0
    fi
    only_sha="${RUN_HEAD_SHA}"
    ;;
esac
jq -r --arg sha "${only_sha}" '
  .[] | select($sha == "" or .headRefOid == $sha)
  | "\(.number)\t\(.headRefOid)\t\(.baseRefName)\t\(.title | gsub("[\\t\\r\\n]"; " "))"
' "${prs}" >"${candidates}"
promote="${work}/promote.txt"
: >"${promote}"
judged=0
green=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r number head base title; do
  [[ -n "${number}" ]] || continue
  if [[ ! "${number}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ || ! "${head}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
    echo "::error::gh pr list returned a malformed pull request: ${number} ${head}"
    exit 1
  fi
  if grep -Eiq '^[[:space:]]*\[swarm\] task_' <<<"${title}"; then
    echo "- #${number} skipped: its title is a \`[swarm] task_\` placeholder, which the gate refuses; retitle it" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
    continue
  fi
  # The base's required checks, the way the gate reads them:
  # classic protection and the effective rules, each name once.
  required="${work}/required-${base//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}.txt"
  if [[ ! -f "${required}" ]]; then
    gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/branches/${base}" >"${work}/branch.json"
    gh api --paginate "repos/${GH_REPO}/rules/branches/${base}" >"${work}/rules.json"
    {
      jq -r '(.protection.required_status_checks.contexts // [])[],
             ((.protection.required_status_checks.checks // [])[] | .context)' "${work}/branch.json"
      jq -rs 'add // [] | .[]
              | select(.type == "required_status_checks")
              | (.parameters.required_status_checks // [])[] | .context' "${work}/rules.json"
    } | awk 'length' | sort -u >"${required}"
  fi
  if [[ ! -s "${required}" ]]; then
    echo "- #${number} not promoted: \`${base}\` has no required checks, so \"every required check passed\" says nothing" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
    continue
  fi
  judged=$((judged + 1))
  gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/commits/${head}/check-runs?per_page=100" >"${work}/check-runs-raw.json"
  jq '.check_runs = [(.check_runs // [])[] | select(.name != "queue for auto-merge")]' \
    "${work}/check-runs-raw.json" >"${work}/check-runs.json"
  gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/commits/${head}/status?per_page=100" >"${work}/status.json"
  # The event of each check suite, read only when some check ran
  # more than once at this head (gate 5's shape): the judge decides
  # a check by the latest run of each event (CHECK-RULE-2).
  printf '{"workflow_runs": []}\n' >"${work}/workflow-runs.json"
  if jq -e '[.check_runs[].name] | group_by(.) | any(length > 1)' "${work}/check-runs.json" >/dev/null; then
    gh api "repos/${GH_REPO}/actions/runs?head_sha=${head}&per_page=100" >"${work}/workflow-runs.json"
  fi
  scripts/merge-train.sh judge --check-runs "${work}/check-runs.json" \
    --statuses "${work}/status.json" --workflow-runs "${work}/workflow-runs.json" \
    --required "${required}" >"${work}/verdict.tsv"
  verdict="$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "verdict" { print $2 }' "${work}/verdict.tsv")"
  case "${verdict}" in
    green)
      green=$((green + 1))
      echo "${number} ${head}" >>"${promote}"
      echo "- #${number} is green at \`${head}\`: marking it \`ready\`" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
      ;;
    pending)
      echo "- #${number} at \`${head}\`: still waiting on its checks" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
      ;;
    red)
      names="$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "failed" { print $2 }' "${work}/verdict.tsv" | sort -u | awk 'NR > 1 { printf ", " } { printf "%s", $0 }')"
      echo "- #${number} is red at \`${head}\`: ${names}" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
      marker="<!-- ready-on-green: red at ${head} -->"
      comments="${work}/comments-${number}.txt"
      gh api --paginate "repos/${GH_REPO}/issues/${number}/comments" --jq '.[].body' >"${comments}"
      if ! grep -qF -- "${marker}" "${comments}"; then
        body="${work}/comment-${number}.md"
        {
          echo "${marker}"
          echo "\`ready-on-green\`: this pull request is red at \`${head}\`, so it was not marked \`ready\`. Failing: ${names}."
          echo
          awk -F'\t' '$1 == "failed" { printf "- [%s](%s)\n", $2, $3 }' "${work}/verdict.tsv"
          echo
          echo "A new head is judged again; the label stays on."
        } >"${body}"
        gh pr comment "${number}" --body-file "${body}"
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      echo "::error::the judge said '${verdict}' for #${number}"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done <"${candidates}"
echo "judged ${judged} ready-on-green pull request(s); ${green} green" | tee -a "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
{
  echo "promote<<PROMOTE_EOF"
  cat "${promote}"
  echo "PROMOTE_EOF"
} >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig --severity HIGH,CRITICAL \
  --ignore-unfixed --format sarif --output trivy-fs.sarif \
  --ignorefile "${RUNNER_TEMP}/trivy-fs.trivyignore.yaml" \
  --exit-code 0 --skip-db-update --no-progress .

render the manifests.run:
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p build/rendered
python3 kubernetes/render.py policies > build/rendered/policies.yaml
python3 kubernetes/render.py tenant --tenant lint > build/rendered/tenant.yaml
profiles="$(python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "apps/common")
from swarm_common.profiles import RUNNER_PROFILES
print(" ".join(sorted(RUNNER_PROFILES)))
PY
)"
for p in ${profiles}; do
  python3 kubernetes/render.py job --tenant lint --profile "${p}" \
    --task tsk_lint --attempt att_lint --lease lease_lint --generation 1 \
    > "build/rendered/job-${p}.yaml"
done
ls -1 build/rendered

scan kubernetes manifests.run:
set -euo pipefail
checkov -d build/rendered --framework kubernetes \
  --skip-check CKV_K8S_14,CKV_K8S_15,CKV_K8S_43 \
  --output cli --output sarif --output-file-path console,checkov-k8s.sarif \
  --compact

scan terraform.run:
set -euo pipefail
checkov -d terraform --framework terraform \
  --output cli --output sarif --output-file-path console,checkov-tf.sarif \
  --compact

scan the current channel images.run:
set -euo pipefail
# scripts/install-trivy.sh says why not trivy's own install.sh.
scripts/install-trivy.sh /usr/local/bin
gcloud auth configure-docker "${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev" --quiet
repo="${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/swarm-images"
status=0
# workspace-apply too: it is the toolchain of swarm-workspace-deployer, the
# one identity here with project-wide account-IAM power (docs/workspaces.md §2.4).
# swarm-live too: the live relay carries a person's keystrokes during a sign-in,
# and ffmpeg is the largest third-party surface any control-plane image ships.
# swarm-egress too (EGRESS-BUILD): it holds the vendor credential and relays
# every proxied browser byte.
# swarm-typesafe-fwd too (SEC-INJECT-B, PR 1385): it holds every tenant's TypeSafe key in memory.
# swarm-graph too (GS-ROLL, part of archived issue 1384): it verifies every agent's graph ticket and serves every tenant's index.
# swarm-voice too (VOICE-ROLL, part of archived issue 2688): it holds the platform owner's OpenAI subscription credential in memory and relays the voice session.
# swarm-github-hooks too (GS-HOOKS, part of archived issue 1384): the one public service, running as the rollup sweeper account.
# swarm-speech too (part of archived issue 2688, docs/design/voice-it-own-speech.md §5.3, §14 L3): the speech machine pulls the digest the release pins, and it carries vLLM and torch, the largest third-party Python surface we ship.
for image in agent-runtime-base agent-runtime-browser agent-runtime-lightpanda agent-runtime-indexer swarm-api swarm-scheduler swarm-quota-broker swarm-reconciler workspace-apply swarm-live swarm-egress swarm-typesafe-fwd swarm-graph swarm-voice swarm-github-hooks swarm-speech; do
  echo "==> ${image}:dev"
  trivy image --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed \
    --exit-code 1 --no-progress "${repo}/${image}:dev" || status=1
done
exit "${status}"

validate-modules.run:
set -euo pipefail
for dir in terraform/modules/*/ terraform/bootstrap/; do
  echo "==> ${dir}"
  terraform -chdir="${dir}" init -backend=false -input=false >/dev/null
  terraform -chdir="${dir}" validate
done

verdict.run:
set -euo pipefail
read -r -a checks <<< "${CHECKS}"
for check in "${checks[@]}"; do
  result="$(printf '%s\n' "${STEPS}" | jq -r --arg check "${check}" '
    [to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("setup-")) | .value.outcome] as $setup
    | [to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith($check + "-")) | .value.outcome] as $own
    | if ($setup | length) == 0 or any($setup[]; . != "success") then "failure"
      elif any($own[]; . == "failure" or . == "cancelled") then "failure"
      elif any($own[]; . == "success") then "success"
      else "skipped" end')"
  echo "${check}: ${result}"
  echo "${check}=${result}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
done

plan.run:
set -euo pipefail
# -out is relative to -chdir, but a shell redirection is not, so both
# derived files are written explicitly under the root.
#
# -lock-timeout=900s, not 120s (archived issue 1874). This job's concurrency group
# serialises terraform.yml's own runs, not a release's apply, so the
# two meet only at the state lock: a main plan that starts during a
# release's "pin, plan, guard, classify and apply" waits for it. That
# step held the lock 108-518 s in the six successful releases read on
# 2026-10-21, and a 120 s wait turned main red for 7b0f769a, a commit
# that broke nothing. 900 s is what hotfix.yml's apply already waits.
# The private values the release passes too (scripts/lib/private-tfvars.sh),
# so main's plan shows no change to the never-touch list or the alerts.
./scripts/lib/private-tfvars.sh --out "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/build/private.tfvars.json"
plan_rc=0
terraform -chdir=${{ env.TF_ROOT }} plan -input=false -lock-timeout=900s \
  -var-file="${SWARM_TFVARS_FILE}" \
  -var-file="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/build/image-refs.tfvars.json" \
  -var-file="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/build/private.tfvars.json" \
  -out=plan.tfplan -no-color > "${TF_ROOT}/plan.txt" 2>&1 || plan_rc=$?
# The plan text holds values from the private tfvars (members, domains,
# addresses), and this repository's logs are public: stdout AND stderr
# (a failed plan's diagnostics quote values too) go to the file, and
# only its summary line and each error's headline reach the log; only
# resource addresses reach the run summary.
grep -E '^(Plan:|No changes)|^((│|\|) )?Error:' "${TF_ROOT}/plan.txt" || true
if [ "${plan_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "::error title=terraform plan failed::exit ${plan_rc}; its error headlines are above, the rest is not printed (the logs are public)"
  exit "${plan_rc}"
fi
terraform -chdir=${{ env.TF_ROOT }} show -json plan.tfplan > "${TF_ROOT}/plan.json"

summarise.run:
{
  echo "### Terraform plan (${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'dev' }})"
  echo
  grep -E '^(Plan:|No changes)' terraform/infra/plan.txt || true
  echo
  echo '```'
  jq -r '.resource_changes[]? | select(.change.actions != ["no-op"] and .change.actions != ["read"]) | "\(.change.actions | join(",")) \(.address | gsub("\\[\"[^\"]*@[^\"]*\"\\]"; "[\"<an address>\"]"))"' terraform/infra/plan.json | head -n 500
  echo '```'
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

say what was not checked.run:
set -euo pipefail
{
  echo "### terraform plan was not run"
  echo
  echo "A pull request's OIDC ref is \`refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge\`."
  echo "The workload identity pool is pinned to \`refs/heads/main\`, so no token"
  echo "is minted here and no plan is possible. That pin is the security boundary:"
  echo "the deployer holds \`resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin\` on a shared project."
  echo
  echo "**Checked on this pull request (offline, no credentials):**"
  echo "- \`terraform fmt -check\`, \`validate\`, \`tflint\`"
  echo "- \`checkov\`"
  echo "- \`terraform test\` over \`tests/terraform\` (86 assertions, mock provider)"
  echo
  echo "**Not checked here:** what the plan would do to the live project."
  echo "That runs on \`main\`, and \`release.yml\` applies it behind an"
  echo "environment approval with the plan attached to read first."
  echo
  echo "A merge queue entry's ref, \`gh-readonly-queue/main/...\`, is not main"
  echo "either: the same holds there."
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
